degree_requirement.value: First degree (e.g. B.Sc. or B.Eng.) in Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics or a closely related area (e.g. Computer Engineering, Informatics) from an internationally recognised university-level institution; additionally one of the listed module profiles must be fulfilled.
degree_requirement.quote: An applicant must have a first degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics or a closely related area awarded by an internationally recognised university-level institution . This can be a Bachelor of Science or Bachelor of Engineering in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Informatics, or other closely related discipline. Additionally, one of the profiles mentioned below must be fulfilled.
degree_requirement.reason: Degree is right but the draft drops the sentence that one of the module profiles must also be fulfilled.

subject_credits.reason: The application page lists module profiles with CP (e.g. Programming 8 CP, Linear Algebra 6 CP) of which one must be fulfilled, but the cleaned text loses which bullets form each profile and the one-of logic does not fit area/min_ects, so a human must read the original page.

value.min_score: 90 points or a total score of 4,5
B2.2.1 or higher (only for students enrolled at RWTH)

english.quote:
a) Test of English as Foreign Language (TOEFL) Internet-based Test (IBT) with a result of at least 90 points or a
total score of 4,5
b) IELTS test with a score of at least 6.0
c) Cambridge Test -B2 First with a grade of at least B
d) Cambridge Test – C1 Advanced
e) Cambridge Test – c2 Proficiency
f) Pearson Test of English (PTE) Academic with a result of at least 60 points
g) UNIcert II or higher
h) a certificate that was acquired as part of the school education required by law in the respective country and
that shows English language skills at level B2 of the "Common European Framework of Reference of Language
(GeR)"1
i) Placement test of the RWTH Language Center with the level B2.2.1 or higher2
english.reason: Draft omits items h) school certificate at CEFR B2 and i) RWTH placement test B2.2.1; footnote 3 also lets Data Science applicants prove English with a Bachelor's thesis or seminar paper in English after Examination Board review, and page 6 exempts degrees/diplomas from UK, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand, Canada or the US.

value.min_scores: quantitative reasoning score: above 75th percentile (among 25% best), verbal reasoning score: above 15th percentile (among 85% best), analytical writing: minimum score 3.5

entrance_tests.quote: You need a Graduate Record Examination (GRE) General Test result that meets all of the following requirements (see exception below) : quantitative reasoning score: above 75th percentile (among 25% best) verbal reasoning score: above 15th percentile (among 85% best) analytical writing: minimum score 3.5 The GRE general test result must be provided with the application for admission before the application for admission deadline. It cannot be handed in after the application for admission deadline. Exception : The GRE is not required for applicants with citizenship of the European Union or European Economic Area or who completed their secondary education in Germany (to be more precise, they have to be what is called “ Bildungsinländerinnen oder Bildungsinländer ” in German, meaning you have an Abitur or equivalent).
entrance_tests.reason: GRE and scores are right, but the exemption is by EU/EEA citizenship or German secondary education (Bildungsinlaender), not by degree country, so listing EU/EEA/Germany as exempt degree countries would wrongly exempt non-EU citizens holding an EU degree; the schema needs a citizenship field to carry this exemption.

value: Copy of transcript of records or diploma supplement (all semesters studied; grades for all but the last two semesters)
Module catalog or course descriptions of all completed courses
For a higher-semester start: final academic transcript (e.g. bachelor's transcript) and a transcript of master's-level studies
GRE General Test result (required by the Data Science examination board)
Certified translation into German or English plus a copy of the original for documents not issued in German or English
required_documents.quote:
Please upload the following documents as PDFs at the end of your application:

- Copy of your transcript of records or your diploma supplement. Please submit a transcript of records with all the semesters you have studied. When you apply you have to be able to provide grades for all the semesters you have studied except your last two semesters of study.

- A module catalog or course descriptions of all the courses you completed in your studies. If these are available on your university’s webpage, you can also upload a PDF that shows the link to this page. If you do not, or cannot upload a module catalog, the respective Examination Board will still review your application for your eligibility for your chosen course(s) of study. Your application may however have to be rejected due to your missing module catalog.

- If you are applying to start in an higher course semester (“advanced standing”): a copy of your final academic transcript (e.g., bachelor’s degree transcript) and a transcript from your master’s level studies.

- Resume (list format)

- You may need to upload additional documents if they are required by the examination board of your master’s program (e.g., proof of the Graduate Record Examination (GRE) , Test AS).
required_documents.reason: Draft omits the higher-semester transcripts from the same list and the certified translations required by the 'Translation of Your Documents' section of the same page.
